Hi Sandra — thanks for the clear ask and the SKU file. Looping in Laura for invoice/evidence detail.

Short answer up front: consolidating into a single metered node-hour SKU simplifies billing but typically reduces line-item visibility for resellers; that tends to drive two common approaches on netback:

1) Maintain a percentage-based commission on list price and apply it to the consolidated SKU (keeps resellers' economics stable but requires a clear mapping doc so commissions are not lost in aggregation).
2) Move to a fixed uplift per node-hour for the reseller (easier to reconcile for distributors who need deterministic per-unit payouts).

Factors that influence which we recommend: expected usage variance, whether reseller requires invoice-level line items for downstream billing, and whether reserved capacity discounts are being applied at the platform level or via credits on the invoice.

Next steps we suggest:
- Ben to propose a netback math example with both % and fixed-uplift approaches.
- Laura to confirm how Redistribute (our invoice routing) will surface the consolidated SKU and what evidence (line-item exports) the reseller will receive.
- We can then produce a 1-page note you can forward to your reseller.

Sandra / Irene — quick draft of the netback math below. I've attached a short PDF with a worked example as well.

Assumptions (example):
- Current: 4 SKUs (A,B,C,D) total list price = €1,000; reseller commission = 10% (they keep €100)
- Consolidated: single node-hour SKU with list price aggregated = €900 (we apply reserved discount at platform level, so list shows €900)

Option A — Percentage commission on consolidated SKU:
List = €900
Reseller commission @10% = €90
Reseller netback = €810
Impact vs current = -€10 (i.e., small reduction)

Option B — Fixed uplift per node-hour (assume expected volume gives uplift equivalent to €95 total):
List = €900
Reseller uplift = €95
Reseller netback = €805
Impact vs current = -€5

Observations:
- Percentage approach scales automatically with price changes and is simplest if reseller wants a line-of-sight percentage.
- Fixed uplift is more predictable month-to-month for the reseller but requires agreeing an expected volume band or true-up cadence.
- If you apply reserved capacity discounts at the platform (Redwood) and show them as invoice credits rather than reducing list, resellers prefer % commissions (they see the gross list and can calculate their cut). If discounts reduce list directly, a fixed uplift often preserves absolute margin for resellers.

Invoice/evidence: Laura — can we confirm whether our invoice export will include both the consolidated SKU and the pre-discount list price (so resellers get a gross-to-net view)? If not, we'll recommend we publish a mapping CSV with gross list + discount columns for BlueArc to share with their partner.

Irene — happy to join the call. Sandra — if you want, I can prepare the one-page note for your reseller after Laura confirms the export fields.
